maya (Docs): Hey folks — opened a small PR to update the model catalog card for mistral-7b (supported runtimes, sequence limits, and benchmarks). link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4212

maya (Docs): Main changes: add 2k/4k token limit notes, note quantized int8 vs fp16 perf, add SDK snippet for streaming with `client.chat.stream` and a short compatibility blurb for CPU fallback.

sam (ML): thanks — can you paste the benchmark numbers here? I want to double-check the latency/throughput before we publish.

maya (Docs): sure, copied from the PR description: 
```
GPUs: A100-40GB (fp16): 16 tokens/s @ 512 context (single-stream)
GPUs: A100-40GB (int8): 24 tokens/s @ 512 context (single-stream)
CPU fallback (intel 8365): ~1.8 tokens/s @ 512 (best-effort, increased latency)
```

sam (ML): those look right-ish but the A100 fp16 single-stream number should be 18 tokens/s (we re-benchmarked last week). Also call out that int8 numbers depend on kernel availability — on older runtimes int8 might not be enabled and you'll see fp16 perf.

maya (Docs): updated the PR to 18 tokens/s and added a sentence about kernel/runtime dependency. also added the SDK snippet for streaming with an explicit `model_variant: "fp16"` param.

taylor (ProdEng): small note: we rolled out a runtime change that renames "int8" variant to "int8-compat" in the routing table for a short window. Could we phrase it like "int8 (aka int8-compat on some clusters)" so customers don't get confused during rollouts?

sam (ML): +1 to taylor. Also add a short compatibility line: "Quantized models may have small token-delta differences vs fp16; use regression evals if exact parity is required."

maya (Docs): done — added both lines. Also added a migration tip under compatibility: "If your app relies on exact logits, pin `model_variant=fp16` while migrating to int8 variants."

ai-ci-bot: Build status — docs PR #4212: checks passing ✅ (link: https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/4212)

maya (Docs): Quick request — can someone from runtime/infra give the final ok on the "limits" wording? I want to avoid implying hard guarantees for dedicated customers.

taylor (ProdEng): Approved wording for hosted docs. Suggest adding parenthetical: "limits listed are for hosted environments; Dedicated/Private deployments can have different limits — check your deployment config."

maya (Docs): added parenthetical. Also fixed a dead link to the SDK example (was pointing to the old repo path).

sam (ML): LGTM, please squash commits and assign to release branch `stable-docs` after merge window opens tomorrow morning.

maya (Docs): will do. tagging @taylor for final go/no-go before I merge.

taylor (ProdEng): go for it after squashing. :thumbsup:

maya (Docs): thanks all! I'll merge after the sqash and then open a tiny migration-note followup to add an example of the `model_variant` override in the Python SDK.

sam (ML): great, and can you add a one-liner in the changelog so PMs see it?

maya (Docs): yup — added to the changelog file in the PR. closing the loop here. :white_check_mark:
